headline: High: open-webui can ingest broad external content and Plane can act on shared files/notes, creating default-path prompt injection, leakage, and cascading workflow risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: open-webui exposes MCP/OpenAPI tools, browsers, and shared persistent sessions, so it can ingest attacker-controlled content by default; Plane accepts file uploads and hyperlinks, which can carry malicious instructions into downstream workflows. The pair has a plausible bridge even without a documented direct integration, so uncertainty pushes severity up.
conditions: IF Plane content is copied into open-webui chats or tools without provenance checks, injection is possible.
IF open-webui is connected to an MCP/OpenAPI server that forwards Plane content, attacker-controlled text can steer tool use.
mitigations: Disable or restrict MCP/OpenAPI connectors for untrusted Plane content.
Require manual review before pasting Plane notes or issue text into open-webui.
Add a provenance banner for imported files and hyperlinks.
Use separate workspaces/accounts for the two agents.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction-stripping at the integration boundary.

B_data_leakage.rationale: open-webui touches files, persistent memory, API keys, and broad network egress; Plane touches files, notes, issues, and hyperlinks. If they share a workspace or file path, sensitive material can flow from one to the other, but the profiles do not show a default shared filesystem or direct sync, so this stays medium.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mounted directory, file contents can leak across them.
IF open-webui uploads local files or API-key-bearing artifacts into its backend, Plane-linked content may be exposed.
mitigations: Separate storage locations for each agent.
Remove secrets from any shared files before upload.
Turn off automatic file import/sync between systems.
Use distinct accounts and API keys.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent access controls on the shared volume.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: open-webui can write via mounted data volumes and spawn subprocesses, while Plane explicitly has write_filesystem=false and no write scopes. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely; the main overlap is read-side coordination, so the pair is low risk here.
conditions: IF Plane is deployed with additional filesystem write privileges not shown here, conflict risk increases.
IF both are given the same mutable directory through an external orchestrator, contention can occur.
mitigations: Keep Plane read-only relative to open-webui-managed files.
Avoid shared mutable directories.
Use file locks if a shared directory is unavoidable.
Schedule writes in separate maintenance windows.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking for shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: open-webui can generate content from prompts, files, and tools, and Plane handles issues/tasks that may be acted on operationally. If Plane consumes open-webui output as authoritative, mistakes can cascade into incorrect tickets or scheduling actions; no verification step is documented, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF Plane imports open-webui-generated text into issues or tasks without human review, errors can propagate.
IF open-webui is used to summarize or classify operational data that Plane then treats as ground truth, cascading error occurs.
mitigations: Require human approval before creating or updating Plane items from open-webui output.
Mark AI-generated text as untrusted in Plane.
Add a verification checklist for imported summaries.
Limit open-webui output to drafts only.
requires-engineering: implement source-attribution and confidence metadata end-to-end.

E_compliance.rationale: open-webui handles API keys, persistent memory, and files, while Plane handles issues, tasks, and files. The profiles do not show a residency or certification mismatch, so only a low compliance concern remains from mixed retention and logging practices on shared data classes.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in both systems with different retention settings, compliance drift can occur.
IF API keys or sensitive notes are copied from open-webui into Plane, retention obligations may diverge.
mitigations: Do not store regulated data in both systems.
Align retention settings before use.
Redact secrets from copied notes.
Review logging defaults in both deployments.
requires-engineering: document and enforce a shared retention policy.
